text:
ana: Morning — async standup. What I did: finished the routing policy e2e tests for header-based sharding, pushed a patch to the gateway config. Blockers: still seeing intermittent 429 spikes in canary that I couldn't reproduce locally. Today: investigate throttling metrics and discuss fallback behavior.

sam: Nice. Can you paste the policy snippet you used for header sharding?

ana: (typo) meant @ana :sweat_smile:

ana: snippet is below — quick copy:

```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "match": { "type": "header", "header": "x-customer-tier", "values": ["premium", "standard"] },
  "buckets": [ {"name": "premium", "pool": "dedicated-1"}, {"name": "standard", "pool": "shared-2"} ],
  "fallback": { "pool": "shared-2", "on_no_match": "route_default" }
}
```

lee: Thanks. For the 429s, can we confirm whether those are per-second or per-minute limiters? Dashboard shows bursts at 5s resolution.

morgan: I put a quick alert on the canary: rate_limit_429_rate > 10/min -> paging. Will follow if it fires.

raj: FYI, the quota service was rotated yesterday at 03:10 UTC for keystore refresh — double-checking whether token caches were flushed. Could cause short-lived 429s.

ana: Good catch. I also saw some spikes around 03:12 in logs. @ana, can you run a targeted query for client_id = rci-frontend between 03:00-03:20?

ana: running now. Quick grep showed a handful of 429s with decorated reason "quota_exceeded" and one with "burst_limit".

sam: If it's quota_exceeded, could be quota window mismatch between gateway and quota service. Are we still using the legacy window aggregation?

ana: We are on the new sliding window for most routes but /v1/generate had a fallback to bucketed windows on canary. I pushed a PR to switch it to sliding — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4123

lee: Tagged the PR for review. Quick comments: ensure the rate-limiter config has tolerant=false only for authenticated premium requests; for unauthenticated we should keep tolerant=true so we return 429 with X-RateLimit info, not drop.

morgan: Also double-check redis timeout settings. If quota read times out, gateway currently treats as deny-by-default. We had a mitigation a year ago to treat timeouts as allow-with-warning for low-priority routes. Might be worth re-enabling.

raj: Agree. Can we make that behavior configurable per route? That way Dedicated customers get strict denies while Hosted can be tolerant.

ana: I can add an opt-in flag 'tolerate_quota_timeouts' to the route metadata. Will add to the PR.

taylor: Blocker for me — code review queue: I need review on the policy rollout orchestration (PR #4119). It's waiting on 2 approvals and someone to sanity check canary rollback.

sam: I'll take a pass after lunch. Quick question for the team: what should the automatic fallback do when the matched pool is at capacity? Current options: redirect to compatible model variant, route to shared pool, or queue. Thoughts?

lee: For latency-sensitive endpoints (generate/chat), prefer redirect to a compatible variant first (e.g., 13B q4 -> 13B fp16). For non-latency-critical batch endpoints, queueing is fine. Document this in the rollout playbook.

morgan: +1. We should also include a metric tag for fallback_reason so we can alert when fallbacks exceed X%.

ana: Adding fallback_reason metric. Also added a tiny change to the gatekeeper so fallback_count increments as a traced event.

deploy-bot: deploy/gateway-canary 2026-03-17T09:35:12Z succeeded (sha: b7c8f2) :rocket:

raj: Thanks bot. After that deploy, I'll rerun the canary load test (script: infra/load_tests/rate_spike.sh) and post results by EOD.

sam: Anything blocking the policy merge? Otherwise we can merge the sliding window change + tolerate flag and monitor.

ana: No blockers from me after I push one more test for redis timeout behavior. Expect to merge this afternoon.

taylor: Cool. My plan today: review #4119, coordinate the rollout doc updates, and schedule a short canary postmortem if we see >5% 429s in next 24h.

lee: I'll update the runbook for capacity fallback and add the metric thresholds.

morgan: ping me if you want me to run the synthetic against US-west region.

ana: thanks everyone. I'll update this thread after merge and attach the canary results. :thumbsup:
